This petition is filed by the L.R's of deceased Sri.B.Manohara Naidu under Section 166 of M.V. Act,
1989 seeking compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- in respect of his death in Road Traffic Accident.
. It is stated in the petition that, 1 st petitioner is the wife, 2nd petitioner is the son, respondent No.3 is the daughter, petitioners no.3 and 4 are parents of the deceased.

That on 18.11.2024 at about 12.45 p.m B.Manohara Naidu was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.PY-01/AY- 5407, on Pakala - Paturu road, Pathalapattu, Chittoor Dist., when he reached near Ayyappagaripalli Outskirts at K.Amarnath Mango Garden, at that time, driver of Bajaj Maxima Auto bearing Reg.No.AP-39/TB-0899, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed from opposite direction and dashed against said B.Manohara Naidu's vehicle and caused accident.
Due to said impact, said B.Manohara Naidu fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Govt., Hospital, Pakala and died in the said hospital during the course of treatment.
Later on Postmortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to his family members.

Petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
transportation of dead body and for performing the last rites.
3. Prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was working as doing Agriculture work, Milk vendor, and rented one JCB on rent basis and earning Rs.90,000/- per month.

sentences.text: The accident is due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Bajaj Maxima Auto bearing Reg.No.AP-39/TB-0899.
The complaint has been (SCCH-12) 4 MVC No.9557/2024 lodged in Puthalapattu UPS Police Station in Cr.No.141/2024 under Section 281, 106(1) of BNS against driver of said vehicle.
Respondent no.1 being RC owner and respondent no.2 being insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
On all these grounds petitioners prayed to award compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with costs and interest in the above case.
4. On issuance of notice, respondent no.1 to 3 are served.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent no.1 and 3 did not appear before the tribunal, they remained absent, hence they are placed exparte.
Respondent no.2 appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
5. 2nd respondent insurance company in its written statement contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
That Sec.134 (C) and Sec.158(6) of MV Act is not complied.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in favour of 1st respondent in respect of Bajaj Maxima Auto bearing Reg.No.AP-39/TB-0899, this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of policy.
It has denied the involvement of vehicle in the alleged accident.

It is contended that driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective D.L. F.C and Permit to the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It has further contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased.
The age, occupation and income of deceased are (SCCH-12) 5 MVC No.9557/2024 denied.
On all these grounds this respondent has prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed following;
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LR's of one Manohara Naidu and competent persons to file this petition?

2. Whether petitioners prove that on 18.11.2024 at about 12.45 PM, husband of 1st petitioner was riding Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.PY-01-AY-5407 near Ayyappagarapalli, outskirts, at K.Amaranath Mango Garden, Patalapattu on Pakala-Paturu Road, Chittor one Auto bearing Reg,
No.AP-39-TB-0899 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed to the motor cycle ridden by Manohar Naidu and caused accident, due to which Manohar Naidu sustained grievous injuries and died while he was taking treatment due to the injuries sustained in the accident?
3.
Whether the petitioners and 3rd respondent are entitled for compensation?
If so by whom and what is the quantum?
4 . What Order or Award?

In case of self employed 25% of the income has to be added to the monthly income to the age group between 40-50 years.
Age of the deceased in this case is 48 years at the time of accident.

Therefore, monthly income of deceased is Rs.16,500/- + 4,125/- =

As such, loss of dependency of the petitioners due to the death of their family member is Rs.24,13,164/-.
18. Loss of love and affection:
Petitioners being L.R's of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their family member.
Therefore, for loss of love and affection compensation has to be granted.

There is no hard and fast rule in respect of measuring love and affection but, in the opinion of this court if amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded for loss of love and affection, the interest of justice would be met.
Accordingly, amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
19. Loss of Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses:

As per the judgment in Pranay Sethi's case, the quantum of compensation for Loss of Consortium is fixed @ Rs.40,000/- and loss of estate and funeral expenses is fixed @ Rs.15,000/- respectively and it is revisable at 10% every 3 years.

As such, accident having taken place in the year 2024, under the head of loss of estate Rs.18,150/-, for funeral expenses Rs.18,150/- and for loss of consortium Rs.48,400/- each to petitioner No.1 to 4 and respondent no.3 is awarded.

sentences.text: As per the petition the respondent no.1 is the RC Owner and respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent no.2 has taken specific contention that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending vehicle had not possessed valid Permit and R.C to ply the said vehicle on road.
Hence he contended that they are not liable to indemnify the respondent no.1.
The respondent no.2 got examined its Senior Manager as RW.1 and he has filed affidavit in lieu of examination in chief, wherein he has reiterated the contention of the written statement.

21. In the cross examination RW.1, petitioner suggested that at the time of issuance of policy it is the duty of insurance company to verify R.C. Permit, Proposal form and Physical inspection of the vehicle for which RW1 stated that it is not mandatory always.

Further he denied the suggestion that,
(SCCH-12) 12 MVC No.9557/2024 though insurance company was aware that there was no valid RC and Permit to aforesaid auto, still the policy was issued to it.
Petitioner contended that since there is implied contract 2 nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner.

22. On the contrary 2nd respondent has relied upon the decision in MFA.No.100628/2020 (MV-D)
of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to the effect that when policy condition is violated, owner is liable.
It is necessary to notice that petitioner is third party to the contract of insurance.

Hence in the opinion of this court insurance company has to indemnify the insured and pay commination to petitioners, but since owner has not produced the permit, nor made any efforts to counter the case of insurance company, the existence of permit is not proved by the owner.
Hence he has to refund the amount to insurance company on the principle of pay and recovery.
Accordingly, this issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.4:
Petitioners have sought for compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- in respect of death of B. Manohara Naidu in road traffic accident.
As per the settled law, the interest that could be awarded on the compensation is only 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till the payment.

Petitioner and Respondent No. 3 being LR's of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 40:20:10:10:20 Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
(SCCH-12) 13 MVC No.9557/2024 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,41,464/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.

In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.2 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 60 days months from the date of this order.
2nd respondent is entitled to recover the entire compensation with interest deposited from the hands of 1st respondent owner of vehicle on the principle of pay and recovery.

Petitioner and Respondent No. 3 being LR's of the deceased are entitled for compensation in the apportionment of 40:20:10:10:20 Hence, I proceed to pass the following;
(SCCH-12) 13 MVC No.9557/2024 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners u/Sec.166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
It is held that, petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.27,41,464/- with interest @ 6%
p.a. on the said amount from the date of petition till the date of payment.
In view of valid insurance policy, respondent no.2 shall indemnify the insured and hereby directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this court within 60 days months from the date of this order.
2nd respondent is entitled to recover the entire compensation with interest deposited from the hands of 1st respondent owner of vehicle on the principle of pay and recovery.
On such deposit, entire compensation awarded to Petitioner no.2 to 4 and respondent No. 3 shall be released in their favour without making F.D and 50% of compensation awarded to 1 st petitioner wife shall be kept in F.D in her name in any nationalized bank of her (SCCH-12) 14 MVC No.9557/2024 choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 50% shall be released in her favour.
The Advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Award be drawn accordingly.
